# Additions to Esther Chapter 4 (Addition D) — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther D | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_004_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition D: Esther's approach to the king. This replaces and expands Hebrew Esther 5:1-2. In the Greek, Esther's approach is far more dramatic: she faints, God intervenes to soften the king's spirit.]*

**4:1** And it-came-to-pass on-the third day, when she-had-ceased praying, that she-removed her garments of mourning and put-on her glorious [clothing].

**4:2** And having-become glorious and having-called upon God the-overseer and savior of all, she-took two maidservants,

**4:3** and upon one she-leaned as though luxuriating because-of softness, and the-other followed carrying her train.

**4:4** And she-was radiant with the-beauty of her appearance, and her face was glad, as one beloved, but her heart was in-anguish because-of fear.

**4:5** And having-entered through all the-doors, she-stood before the-king. And he-was seated upon the-throne of his kingdom, clothed with his whole garment of manifestation — golden and precious stones — and he-was in-great-awe.

**4:6** And having-lifted his face, inflamed with glory, he-looked at her with rage. And the-queen fell and changed-color, and having-bent she-rested herself upon the-head of the-maidservant who-went-before her.

**4:7** And God changed the-spirit of the-king to-gentleness, and being-anxious he-leaped from his throne and caught her in his arms, until she-came-to-herself, and he-comforted her with words of peace, and said to her:

**4:8** "What is it, Esther? I am your brother. Take-courage!

**4:9** You-shall-not die; for our arrangement is common. Come near."

**4:10** And raising the-golden scepter he-laid it upon her neck, and he-embraced her and said:

**4:11** "Speak to me."

**4:12** And she-said to him: "I saw you, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled because-of fear of your glory.

**4:13** For you are marvelous, my lord, and your face is full of grace."

**4:14** And while she-was speaking, she-fainted and fell; and the-king was-troubled, and all his servants comforted her.
